one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the window: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29 (10:00 ET call). Consensus is about $9.8-9.9 EPS on $22.1-22.4B revenue, below Q2's $23.0B, so the bar looks beatable: Q2 beat by about $1.8-2.3 despite $3.03 of IPR&D, Foundayo is at ~47.5k weekly scripts (+8% w/w to Sep 11, IQVIA via Guggenheim) rather than the 34k I used, and Ricks reports 700k Medicare Bridge starts with 70% on Lilly. The base rate still says there is little edge in earnings direction: Trefis counts 19 earnings days over five years, 53% up, medians +4.5% / -3.5%. I drop the round-1 'fell like a rock' framing: daily closes show September was flat ($1,156.73 on Aug 31 to $1,157.08 on Sep 30), so there is no oversold rebound or fresh shock to price. The TRIUMPH-2 EASD data (Sep 30, -2.3%) is behind us; the 7th Circuit retatrutide opinion could land at any time but courts take weeks to months, and the CagriSema decision most likely falls around mid-December. Median about $1,153 (+0.3%); spread is 80% lognormal at sigma 9% and 20% at sigma 15%, which averages to about the 10% monthly vol from 35%/3.5 with fatter tails for a possible earnings gap.

fair_value.method: Blend of (1) 22.5x NTM EPS at Oct 2027 of $51.6 (0.25 x 2027 consensus $47.5 + 0.75 x 2028E $53.0) = $1,161, weight 50%; (2) 26x TTM EPS at Oct 2027 of $44.65 = $1,161, weight 30%; (3) base-rate drift $1,149.85 x 1.04 = $1,196, weight 20%. Blend $1,168, rounded to $1,170.

Published 2028 consensus is $51.0-52.7 (MarketScreener $51.01 on +11.6% revenue; 24/7 $52.29; an aggregate $51.34 / 8 analysts). I put it slightly above the midpoint, at $53.0 (2027 x 1.116), because MarketScreener's 2027 figure ($44.49) is stale against the $47.51 now on StockAnalysis, revisions run 19 up / 4 down, and Guggenheim just raised Foundayo to $1.8B in 2027 and $3.7B in 2028. I no longer use my $55.3 (x1.17), which sat above every published figure.

About 24.2x 2027 EPS today. The 5-year average forward P/E is about 41x, but growth is slowing toward ~11-12% in 2028. Peers are much cheaper (Novo 12x, Merck 15x), and the Arnott 'top dog' studies find the sector leader lags by 3-4% a year. Unchanged from round 1: the supervisor's corrections hit EPS, not the multiple.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 2026 plus Q1-Q3 2027, approximated as 0.94 x 2027 consensus of $47.5

GuruFocus 10-year TTM P/E median is 42.7 (range 21.4-263); I cut it hard for slowing growth and the Gilead/Novo de-rating analogs. Lowered from 27x so it matches the P/E leg: 22.5x NTM on $51.6 vs TTM $44.65 implies ~26x TTM. 27x would assume ~20% forward growth, against ~11-12% 2028 consensus revenue growth (id 42).

Equity return of about 7-8%, less the 3-4% a year by which the largest company in a sector has historically lagged its sector (Arnott and Wu). I have dropped the recession prediction-market inputs (ids 10, 11) as drivers, per the supervisor: macro odds add little for a low-beta pharma name.

bear.story: Price erosion outruns volume after the January 2027 resets (Novo $675 list, CVS co-preferred, $245 Medicare). MFN goes beyond Medicaid, the Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor (BALANCE Part D delayed indefinitely), Foundayo stays a distant second, and the 7th Circuit upholds NDA status (base rate favours the FDA: only ~8-14% of merits appeals reverse). 2027 EPS is cut toward $42 and the multiple falls to about 19x, in a partial replay of Gilead 2016 (-29%) or Novo 2024-26 (-74%).

base.story: Volume keeps outrunning price. 2027 EPS lands near $47.5, 2028 consensus drifts to about $53, the retatrutide BLA goes in during Q1 2027 with approval most likely around the end of 2027 or early 2028 (outside or at the edge of the horizon), and by Oct 2027 the stock trades at about 22.5x NTM EPS of $51.6, with the 2028 Medicare cliff weighing on the multiple.

bull.story: Revisions keep running up (2027 consensus $41.9 in April to $47.5 now), Foundayo's share of new oral starts (one-third per Ricks) turns into total-script share, and retatrutide gets a national-priority voucher and is approved by mid-2027. Kalshi prices that at about 45% before Jul 2027, but the market is thin and I weight it below that. 2028 EPS is about $57, NTM about $56, and the stock trades at about 27x, short of Citi's $1,600.

thesis_break_reason: $850 is about 26% below today and 17.9x 2027 consensus EPS of $47.5, below anything LLY has traded at on forward earnings in the GLP-1 era and below the lowest Street target ($930). LLY's recent worst drawdowns were about 34% (Aug 2025) and 23% (2026) without broken fundamentals, so the break is the level plus estimate cuts, with 2027/2028 consensus falling toward ~$42/$45. Likely causes: US net price falling well past Q2's -9% underlying after the Jan 2027 resets, MFN reaching commercial pricing, no Medicare successor to the Bridge, a retatrutide safety or regulatory setback, or clear share loss to oral or next-gen rivals. I keep $850 rather than the supervisor's $840; the gap is within rounding.

key_uncertainties: US GLP-1 net-price erosion (MFN, DTC, Novo price war, Jan 2027 resets) compared with volume growth
Whether 2028 EPS tracks the ~$51-53 consensus or the revision momentum carries it higher
Foundayo: ~47.5k weekly scripts and one-third of new oral starts, but ~1:3.5-4 in total oral scripts vs the Wegovy pill
Retatrutide approval timing (standard review points to around end-2027; a voucher would pull it into the horizon) and the 7th Circuit classification ruling
Medicare coverage cliff after the Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor
Whether the multiple de-rates like Novo's or Gilead's as growth slows (top-dog base rates)
Recurring acquired-IPR&D charges flowing into non-GAAP EPS
reasoning: Base rates first, unchanged from round 1: 35% realized vol, near-symmetric earnings-day reactions (53% up, medians +4.5% / -3.5%), annual max drawdowns of 15-34%, a 3-4% a year top-dog lag, and Gilead 2016 / Novo 2024-26 as left-tail analogs. The supervisor's corrections, which I verified and accept: (a) 2028 consensus EPS is $51-53 (MarketScreener $51.01, 24/7 $52.29, an aggregate $51.34), not my $55.3; I now use $53.0, giving NTM $51.6. (b) Foundayo is ~47.5k weekly scripts to Sep 11 (IQVIA via Guggenheim), not 34k; this is mildly positive and supports putting 2028 at the top of the consensus range. (c) September was flat, not a sell-off. (d) Medicare Bridge has 700k starts, 70% on Lilly, and ends 2027-12-31 with no successor. On Kalshi I partly disagree. I re-read the market through Kalshi's public API, so it is now verified: before Jul 2027 at 43-46c (13.2k contracts traded) and before Jan 2028 at 87-88c, but on only 2.5k contracts, which is thin. Lilly still guides to a Q1 2027 BLA, a standard review points to around end-2027, and no voucher has been announced. So I treat ~35% as the chance of approval inside the horizon and no longer let the 90% carry the base case. That trims the bull price from $1,560 to $1,500. The 7th Circuit appeal is a binary for the terminal multiple; the base rate for reversal on appeal is low (~8-14% of merits appeals), so the NDA outcome is closer to the default, and I leave it as a bear-case contributor. I also made the TTM multiple consistent with slower growth (27x to 26x). Fair value moves from $1,200 to $1,170. The distribution is a three-lognormal mixture: bear $810 (22%, sigma 0.28), base $1,165 (56%, sigma 0.21), bull $1,500 (22%, sigma 0.22). Its median is about $1,160 and P(>= spot) is 0.51. No option data was consulted, and nothing under priors/ or round1_capped/ was opened. Round-2 research was 6 web searches plus Kalshi API reads.
